sections.title: The engineering problems unique to AI SaaS

blocks.heading: Tenant data isolation
paragraphs: In AI products, isolation failures are not just access-control bugs — a shared index or prompt context can leak one customer's data into another's answer. We enforce isolation at the storage, retrieval and prompt layers and test for cross-tenant leakage.

blocks.heading: Unit economics and inference cost
paragraphs: Every user action can incur model cost. We meter usage per tenant, route requests to the least expensive model that meets quality, cache aggressively and align pricing tiers with real inference cost so margins hold as you grow.

blocks.heading: Quality you can measure release to release
paragraphs: Evaluation datasets and automated regression tests run whenever prompts, models or retrieval change, so product updates do not silently degrade answer quality for existing customers.

items.question: How much does it cost to build an AI SaaS product?
items.answer: A focused AI SaaS MVP with one core AI feature, basic multi-tenancy and billing typically costs $40,000–$90,000. Products with per-tenant knowledge bases or agent workflows run $65,000–$200,000, and full vertical or enterprise platforms $100,000–$500,000+.

items.question: How long does an AI SaaS MVP take?
items.answer: Most MVPs launch in 12–20 weeks, including discovery, the AI core, authentication, billing and an admin console.

items.question: How do you prevent one customer's data appearing in another's results?
items.answer: We isolate tenant data at the storage, vector index and prompt-construction layers, scope every retrieval to the requesting tenant, and include cross-tenant leakage tests in the automated test suite.

items.question: How do you keep AI costs from destroying margins?
items.answer: Per-tenant usage metering, model routing to cheaper models where quality allows, caching, token budgets and pricing tiers aligned with inference cost. We model unit economics during discovery.

items.question: Can you build on top of OpenAI, Anthropic or open-weight models?
items.answer: Yes. We are model-agnostic and often design a provider abstraction so you can switch or combine models as prices and capabilities change.

items.question: Do we own the product code?
items.answer: Yes — full IP transfer of all source code, infrastructure configuration, evaluation datasets and documentation.
